# stepcadence

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/jhuwit/cadence/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jhuwit/cadence/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/jhuwit/cadence/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/jhuwit/cadence)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of `stepcadence` is to calculate cadence (steps per minute) metrics
from minute-level step count data, following
[Tudor-Locke et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2017-097628):
peak and maximum cadence, mean cadence, and time spent in cadence levels and
bands.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `stepcadence` from
[GitHub](https://github.com/jhuwit/cadence) with:

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jhuwit/cadence")
```

## Example

The input is a data frame with one row per minute and `time` and `steps`
columns.  `summarize_cadence()` computes every metric, here for each
participant (`SEQN`) and day (`PAXDAYM`):

```{r example}
library(stepcadence)
head(simulated_nhanes_steps)

result = summarize_cadence(simulated_nhanes_steps,
                           group_cols = nhanes_group_cols())
result
```

See `vignette("calculate_cadence", package = "stepcadence")` for details on
each metric, cadence bands, and handling non-wear time.
